answer: An anchor for each identity is a karst survey filed with the applicant's one numbered prism, one per verified field licence. The registry assigns a sinkhole; the applicant files its spectrum, depth, and GPS fix, and an auditor re-measures the site within one epoch — a mismatch voids the identity and burns the prism. The k-th identity under one prism needs k fresh surveys in one epoch. Forging 1,000 puppets means 500,500 surveys at $60 each, $30,030,000 of fieldwork; the 1,000th alone costs $60,000. A fresh prism needs a fresh verified human. One honest user files a single $60 survey.
